table.name: Closed Loop Load Limit 1
table.description: Load threshold by engine speed used by closed-loop transition logic.

table.name: Closed Loop Load Limit 2
table.description: Load threshold by engine speed used by closed-loop transition logic.

table.name: Closed Loop Load Limit 3
table.description: Load threshold by engine speed used by closed-loop transition logic.

table.name: Closed Loop Open Loop APP Threshold 1
table.description: Accelerator-pedal position threshold by RPM that triggers transition to open-loop fueling.

table.name: Closed Loop Open Loop APP Threshold 2
table.description: Accelerator-pedal position threshold by RPM that triggers transition to open-loop fueling.

table.name: Closed Loop Open Loop APP Threshold 3
table.description: Accelerator-pedal position threshold by RPM that triggers transition to open-loop fueling.

table.name: Closed Loop Open Loop APP Threshold 4
table.description: Accelerator-pedal position threshold by RPM that triggers transition to open-loop fueling.

table.name: Closed Loop Open Loop APP Threshold 5
table.description: Accelerator-pedal position threshold by RPM that triggers transition to open-loop fueling.

table.name: Closed Loop Open Loop Transition Timer 1
table.description: High-pedal qualification delay at higher barometric pressure. The counter reloads while the pedal condition is clear and counts down in 100 ms steps while it remains active. Other transition conditions still apply.

table.name: Closed Loop Open Loop Transition Timer 1 - Lower Barometric Pressure
table.description: Companion high-pedal qualification delay at lower barometric pressure. Counts down in 100 ms steps while the pedal condition remains active. Other transition conditions still apply.

table.name: Closed Loop Open Loop Transition Timer 2
table.description: Normal warm-engine transition delay at higher barometric pressure. Counts down in 100 ms steps when load or pedal demand qualifies. Other conditions may clear the delay early.

table.name: Closed Loop Open Loop Transition Timer 3
table.description: Normal warm-engine transition delay at lower barometric pressure. Counts down in 100 ms steps when load or pedal demand qualifies. Other conditions may clear the delay early.

table.name: Closed Loop Open Loop Transition Timer - Cold
table.description: Transition delay while the engine is below the factory warm qualification. This bank takes priority over the normal and knock-present banks. Counts down in 100 ms steps when transition conditions are met.

table.name: Closed Loop Open Loop Transition Timer - Knock Present
table.description: Transition delay selected in the warm-engine knock-present mode. Counts down in 100 ms steps when transition conditions are met. The cold bank takes priority.

table.name: Cold Coolant Rev Limiter - 1
table.description: First-priority cold-condition RPM limit. Overrides the secondary cold-condition limit and the normal rev limiter while its qualification is active.

table.name: Cold Coolant Rev Limiter - 2
table.description: Secondary cold-condition RPM limit, used while its hold is active and the first-priority limit is not selected.

table.name: MAF Fault Requested Load Limit
table.description: Additional requested-load ceiling during a qualified MAF signal fault. Applies after the main load multipliers.

table.name: MAF Volts Range Upper Limit Check
table.description: Upper MAF sensor voltage threshold for fault qualification. The high-voltage state requires the sensor check to be enabled. This is a diagnostic threshold, not an airflow limit.

table.name: Maximum Spark Timing
table.description: Maximum permitted ignition timing after the normal timing corrections. Fixed and override timing modes can bypass this clamp.

table.name: Min Desired Lambda/AFR
table.description: Minimum permitted lambda request by engine speed. Lower values allow a richer request. Applies after the normal request and its three correction terms are combined; other fueling corrections and operating modes remain separate.

table.name: Minimum Spark Timing 1
table.description: Minimum permitted ignition timing for this factory-selected mode. Other active timing floors may raise the effective minimum.

table.name: Minimum Spark Timing 2
table.description: Minimum permitted ignition timing for this factory-selected mode. Other active timing floors may raise the effective minimum.

table.name: Minimum Spark Timing 3
table.description: Minimum permitted ignition timing for this factory-selected mode. Other active timing floors may raise the effective minimum.

table.name: Minimum Spark Timing 4
table.description: Minimum permitted ignition timing for this factory-selected mode. Other active timing floors may raise the effective minimum.

table.name: Neutral/Reverse Max Load High BAT
table.description: Neutral/reverse load limit at high boost-air temperatures. Blends with the low-temperature limit.

table.name: Neutral/Reverse Max Load Low BAT
table.description: Neutral/reverse load limit at low boost-air temperatures. Blends with the high-temperature limit.

table.name: Operating Load Limit 1
table.description: Normal operating-load ceiling by RPM. MAF fault operation bypasses this ceiling and uses separate fault limiting.

table.name: Operating Load Limit 2
table.description: Alternate operating-load ceiling by RPM. Used only when the alternate mode is selected and its inhibit is clear.

table.name: Overboost Protection Fuel Cut
table.description: Manifold pressure threshold for protective fuel cut, by engine speed and barometric pressure. The protection delay and RPM qualification still apply.

table.name: Overload Protection Fuel Cut
table.description: Load threshold for protective fuel cut, by engine speed and intake-air temperature. The protection delay and RPM qualification still apply.

table.name: Overload Timing Mode - Load Threshold
table.description: Load threshold that can request the factory overload timing mode. Overload timing and retard tables determine the timing change. Other qualification and priority conditions still apply. This is not a requested-load ceiling.

table.name: Rev Limiter Normal
table.description: Normal-condition maximum engine RPM before fuel cut.

table.name: RPM Range Upper Limit Check
table.description: Maximum engine speed for normal MAF high-voltage fault qualification. Above this speed, or while its other inhibit conditions are active, the ECU resets the high-voltage qualification counters. This does not set the rev limiter.

table.name: Speed Limiter - Fuel Cut
table.description: Vehicle-speed threshold for the fuel-cut request. The separate RPM qualification and other enable conditions must also be met.

table.name: Speed Limiter - Throttle Close
table.description: Vehicle-speed setpoint for limiting pedal demand and closing the throttle. RPM qualification and other enable conditions also apply.

table.name: Speed Limiter Threshold - Fuel Cut
table.description: Speed drop below the fuel-cut setpoint that clears its speed request. This is a hysteresis amount, not a second absolute speed setpoint.

table.name: Speed Limiter Threshold - Throttle Close
table.description: Speed drop below the throttle-limiting setpoint that clears its limiting state. RPM and inhibit conditions can also clear it. This is a hysteresis amount, not a second absolute speed setpoint.

table.name: APP Mapping 1st Gear
table.description: Remaps accelerator-pedal demand for 1st gear. Factory priority and alternate pedal modes can override this bank.

table.name: APP Mapping 2nd Gear
table.description: Remaps accelerator-pedal demand for 2nd gear. Factory priority and alternate pedal modes can override this bank.

table.name: APP Mapping 3rd Gear
table.description: Remaps accelerator-pedal demand for 3rd gear. Factory priority and alternate pedal modes can override this bank.

table.name: APP Mapping 4th Gear
table.description: Remaps accelerator-pedal demand for 4th gear. Factory priority and alternate pedal modes can override this bank.

table.name: APP Mapping 5th Gear
table.description: Remaps accelerator-pedal demand for 5th gear. Factory priority and alternate pedal modes can override this bank.

table.name: APP Mapping 6th Gear
table.description: Remaps accelerator-pedal demand for 6th gear. Factory priority and alternate pedal modes can override this bank.

table.name: APP Mapping Neutral
table.description: Remaps accelerator-pedal demand for neutral. Factory priority and alternate pedal modes can override this bank.

table.name: APP Mapping Reverse
table.description: Remaps accelerator-pedal demand in reverse. Factory priority and alternate pedal modes can override this bank.

table.name: APP Multiplier Speed Adjustment
table.description: Multiplier applied after the gear-specific pedal map, based on pedal position and vehicle speed. The same grid adjusts current and retained pedal requests. Values below 1 reduce demand.

table.name: BCS Correction Mode
table.description: Engine load (0) corrects boost-solenoid duty using the difference between actual and target engine load, with overboost correction when its pressure limit is exceeded. Boost pressure (1, or any nonzero value) uses the difference between actual and target pressure. This selection does not enable the separate alternate targeting strategy.

table.name: BCS DC Accumulated Correction Limit - Decrease
table.description: Limits accumulated duty reduction. More negative values allow more reduction. Overall correction and final duty limits still apply.

table.name: BCS DC Accumulated Correction Limit - Increase
table.description: Limits accumulated duty increase. Raising this value allows more accumulated positive correction. Overall correction and final duty limits still apply.

table.name: BCS DC Adjustment - Boost Limit Exceeded
table.description: Added to accumulated duty correction each update while overboost is latched in load-error mode. Positive values add duty; negative values subtract duty. Correction limits apply. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: BCS DC Adjustment Barometer
table.description: Scales base duty with barometric pressure. 100% leaves base duty unchanged; lower values reduce it and higher values increase it. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: BCS DC Adjustment Battery Voltage
table.description: Adds duty points for battery-voltage compensation. Positive values increase commanded duty; negative values reduce it. Final duty limits apply. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: BCS DC Adjustment Boost Target Correction (Boost Targeting Mode)
table.description: Accumulated duty-point correction from actual pressure minus target pressure. Used when BCS Correction Mode is nonzero. Positive values add duty; negative values subtract duty. Correction and final-duty limits apply. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: BCS DC Adjustment IAT
table.description: Scales base duty with intake air temperature. 100% leaves base duty unchanged; lower values reduce it and higher values increase it. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: BCS DC Adjustment Limit - Decrease
table.description: Lower limit on the initial plus accumulated duty correction. The accumulated correction also has its own limit; final duty remains within 0 to 100 percent.

table.name: BCS DC Adjustment Limit - Increase
table.description: Upper limit on the initial plus accumulated duty correction. The accumulated correction also has its own limit; final duty remains within 0 to 100 percent.

table.name: BCS DC Base
table.description: Base wastegate solenoid duty by RPM and selected throttle input. Higher values increase commanded duty before multipliers, corrections and limits. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: BCS Throttle Input
table.description: 0 uses measured throttle position for the wastegate lookup. Any nonzero value uses the throttle target from the active normal or alternate strategy. The selected input is limited by the lookup axis.

table.name: Boost Limit Barometer Adjustment
table.description: Scales the pressure limit for engine speed and barometric pressure.

table.name: Overboost Pressure Limit - Base
table.description: Base pressure limit for overboost correction. Barometric adjustment scales the limit; hysteresis controls when correction clears.

table.name: Overboost Pressure Limit Hysteresis
table.description: Pressure must fall this far below the limit before overboost correction clears.

table.name: MAP Targets (Boost Targeting Mode)
table.description: Manifold-pressure target for pressure-error boost correction. The pressure-error mode switch is disabled in this ROM's stock configuration.

table.name: Fan On Engine Coolant Temperature
table.description: Coolant-temperature threshold used by fan control at each barometric pressure. The factory temperature estimate and other fan requests still apply. A barometer fault uses the first cell.

table.name: Fan On Voltage Adjustment
table.description: Scales the normal fan-output requests for battery voltage. A value of 1 leaves them unchanged. Each output retains its factory ceiling; override modes can bypass this multiplier.

table.name: Closed Loop AFR Target
table.description: Closed-loop lambda target used by the factory blend. Its companion blend bank also contributes to the baseline fuel target. Lower values request richer fueling. RPM and load outside the axes use the nearest edge.

table.name: Closed Loop AFR Target - Companion Blend Bank
table.description: Companion lambda target on the other side of the factory blend. Keep it consistent with Closed Loop AFR Target unless a mode-specific change is intended. Lower values request richer fueling. RPM and load outside the axes use the nearest edge.

table.name: Clutch Press Timer
table.description: Hold time after a qualifying clutch press, by RPM and the gear captured at the press. Counts down in 5 ms steps and holds the related fuel-cut countdowns at zero while active. Factory qualification and early-clear conditions still apply.

table.name: Cold Cranking and Afterstart Enrichment
table.description: Starting enrichment for this factory-selected bank. The higher cold-start or warmup state is used, then fades with its matching decrement. At coolant temperatures of 203 degF or higher, separate hot-start values replace this curve.

table.name: Cold Cranking and Afterstart Enrichment - Alternate Mode
table.description: Starting enrichment for this factory-selected bank. The higher cold-start or warmup state is used, then fades with its matching decrement. At coolant temperatures of 203 degF or higher, separate hot-start values replace this curve. Used only when the alternate enrichment mode is selected.

table.name: Cold Cranking and Afterstart Enrichment Decrement
table.description: Amount removed from this enrichment state once per full 720-degree engine cycle after cranking. Larger values make it fade faster; elapsed time depends on RPM. At coolant temperatures of 203 degF or higher, separate hot-start values replace this curve.

table.name: Cold Cranking and Afterstart Enrichment Decrement - Alternate Mode
table.description: Amount removed from this enrichment state once per full 720-degree engine cycle after cranking. Larger values make it fade faster; elapsed time depends on RPM. At coolant temperatures of 203 degF or higher, separate hot-start values replace this curve. Used only when the alternate enrichment mode is selected.

table.name: Conditional Fuel Correction - Coolant Factor
table.description: One factor in the conditional fuel correction. All three factors are multiplied together; zero in any factor prevents correction. Factory operating conditions must also allow it.

table.name: Conditional Fuel Correction - RPM Factor
table.description: One factor in the conditional fuel correction. All three factors are multiplied together; zero in any factor prevents correction. Factory operating conditions must also allow it.

table.name: Conditional Fuel Correction - Signal Ratio Factor
table.description: Signal-ratio factor in the conditional fuel correction. All three factors are multiplied together; zero in any factor prevents correction. Factory operating conditions must also allow it.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Requested Load Threshold
table.description: Base load threshold used to release deceleration fuel cut. Other enable conditions, hysteresis and release delays still apply. Also provides the base threshold for selecting deceleration fuel pressure.

table.name: Decel Fuel Cut Requested Load Threshold Additive
table.description: Added to the base load threshold when selecting deceleration fuel pressure. Positive values allow that pressure mode at higher load. This additive does not change the separate fuel-cut release threshold.

table.name: Decel RPM Offset - Base
table.description: RPM above idle used for deceleration thresholds when no alternate setting applies. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Decel RPM Offset - Supplemental
table.description: Additional RPM above idle used as a floor for deceleration thresholds when enabled. Other active RPM floors can take priority. Larger values keep the RPM thresholds higher.

table.name: Enrichment Multiplier - Cold Start and Warmup
table.description: Scales supplemental enrichment while the factory cold-start/warmup multiplier mode is active. A value of 1 leaves it unchanged. Outside that mode the multiplier is 1.

table.name: Enrichment Multiplier - Supplemental
table.description: Scales supplemental enrichment in its conditional mode. Values above 1 increase the request before other offsets and limits. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Fuel Correction Ramp - Maximum RPM
table.description: Maximum RPM gate for a factory fuel correction ramp. This is not the main engine rev limit. The minimum RPM gate and other factory conditions also apply.

table.name: Fuel Correction Ramp - Minimum RPM
table.description: Minimum RPM gate for a factory fuel correction ramp. This is not the main engine rev limit. The maximum RPM gate and other factory conditions also apply.

table.name: Fuel Feedback Gain
table.description: Sets fuel-feedback strength by airflow. Works with the response-period table and factory feedback limits.

table.name: Fuel Feedback Response Period
table.description: Response period used to calculate fuel-feedback corrections by airflow. Larger values reduce the integral term and increase the derivative term. Use positive values. This is a controller setting, not a sensor delay.

table.name: Fuel Specific Gravity
table.description: Fuel density used for fuel-mass and volume calculations. Keep it consistent with the fuel being used. Use a positive value.

table.name: Load Change Fuel Correction - Drop Amount
table.description: Fuel correction during a qualified load drop. Negative values remove fuel. The factory speed gate allows this correction only above 49.7 mph; load weighting and operating gates also apply.

table.name: Load Change Fuel Correction - Rise Offset
table.description: Adds to the fuel correction during a qualified load rise. The rise weighting and operating gates still apply. Zero adds no offset.

table.name: LTFT Adjustment ECT
table.description: Coolant-temperature multiplier for negative long-term fuel trims. Positive trims bypass this correction. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: LTFT Partition 1
table.description: Airflow boundary for long-term fuel-trim learning ranges. Factory hysteresis and operating conditions also affect range selection. Keep the boundaries in ascending order; matching upper boundaries leave those ranges inactive.

table.name: LTFT Partition 2
table.description: Airflow boundary for long-term fuel-trim learning ranges. Factory hysteresis and operating conditions also affect range selection. Keep the boundaries in ascending order; matching upper boundaries leave those ranges inactive.

table.name: LTFT Partition 3
table.description: Airflow boundary for long-term fuel-trim learning ranges. Factory hysteresis and operating conditions also affect range selection. Keep the boundaries in ascending order; matching upper boundaries leave those ranges inactive.

table.name: LTFT Partition 4
table.description: Airflow boundary for long-term fuel-trim learning ranges. Factory hysteresis and operating conditions also affect range selection. Keep the boundaries in ascending order; matching upper boundaries leave those ranges inactive.

table.name: LTFT Partition 5
table.description: Airflow boundary for long-term fuel-trim learning ranges. Factory hysteresis and operating conditions also affect range selection. Keep the boundaries in ascending order; matching upper boundaries leave those ranges inactive.

table.name: LTFT Partition 6
table.description: Airflow boundary for long-term fuel-trim learning ranges. Factory hysteresis and operating conditions also affect range selection. Keep the boundaries in ascending order; matching upper boundaries leave those ranges inactive.

table.name: Open Loop Part Throttle AFR Target Knock Present
table.description: Knock-related-mode open-loop lambda target by RPM and load. Overload takes priority over knock-related mode. Used when the WOT curve is not selected. Lower values command richer fueling. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Open Loop Part Throttle AFR Target Normal
table.description: Normal-mode open-loop lambda target by RPM and load. Overload takes priority over knock-related mode. Used when the WOT curve is not selected. Lower values command richer fueling. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Open Loop Part Throttle AFR Target Overload
table.description: Overload-mode open-loop lambda target by RPM and load. Overload takes priority over knock-related mode. Used when the WOT curve is not selected. Lower values command richer fueling. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Open Loop WOT AFR Target Knock Present
table.description: Knock-related-mode RPM-only lambda target when WOT state is active and its inhibit is clear. Overload takes priority over knock-related mode. Lower values command richer fueling. RPM outside the axis uses the nearest endpoint.

table.name: Open Loop WOT AFR Target Normal
table.description: Normal-mode RPM-only lambda target when WOT state is active and its inhibit is clear. Overload takes priority over knock-related mode. Lower values command richer fueling. RPM outside the axis uses the nearest endpoint.

table.name: Open Loop WOT AFR Target Overload
table.description: Overload-mode RPM-only lambda target when WOT state is active and its inhibit is clear. Overload takes priority over knock-related mode. Lower values command richer fueling. RPM outside the axis uses the nearest endpoint.

table.name: Supplemental Fuel Enrichment - Additional
table.description: Extra fuel enrichment added before the enrichment limit. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Supplemental Fuel Enrichment - Additional Multiplier 1
table.description: Scales additional supplemental enrichment by RPM and load in this factory-selected mode. A value of 1 leaves it unchanged. Load above 1.0 uses the top load row.

table.name: Supplemental Fuel Enrichment - Additional Multiplier 2
table.description: Scales additional supplemental enrichment by RPM and load in this factory-selected mode. A value of 1 leaves it unchanged. Load above 1.0 uses the top load row.

table.name: Supplemental Fuel Enrichment - Base
table.description: Base supplemental fuel enrichment before the load multiplier and enrichment limit. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Supplemental Fuel Enrichment - Limit
table.description: Limits combined supplemental fuel enrichment before the mode multiplier and other corrections. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Supplemental Fuel Enrichment - Load Multiplier 1
table.description: Scales base supplemental enrichment with load in this factory-selected mode. A value of 1 leaves it unchanged. The two mode banks share the same load axis.

table.name: Supplemental Fuel Enrichment - Load Multiplier 1 - Alternate Mode
table.description: Scales base supplemental enrichment with load in this factory-selected mode. A value of 1 leaves it unchanged. The two mode banks share the same load axis.

table.name: Supplemental Fuel Enrichment - Load Multiplier 2
table.description: Scales base supplemental enrichment with load when multiplier mode 2 is selected.

table.name: Timed Fuel Correction - Amount
table.description: Fuel correction loaded after a qualifying mode change while its hold is active. Cranking clears the correction. After the hold expires, the matching decay returns it to zero.

table.name: Timed Fuel Correction - Decay
table.description: Correction removed at each 180-degree crank event after the hold expires. Elapsed time depends on RPM. This is separate from the cold-start and warmup fade, which updates once per full engine cycle.

table.name: Timed Fuel Correction - Hold Time
table.description: Time to hold the correction after a qualifying mode change. Counts down in 25 ms steps. Release conditions can end the hold early.

table.name: Transition Fuel Correction - Amount
table.description: Fuel correction loaded after a qualifying factory mode transition. This ROM uses a single amount for all coolant temperatures. Operating and transition gates still apply.

table.name: Transition Fuel Correction - Amount Decay
table.description: Correction removed once per full 720-degree engine cycle while this correction returns to zero. Larger values make it fade faster. This ROM uses a single decay amount for all coolant temperatures.

table.name: Warmup Enrichment
table.description: Starting enrichment for this factory-selected bank. The higher cold-start or warmup state is used, then fades with its matching decrement. At coolant temperatures of 203 degF or higher, separate hot-start values replace this curve.

table.name: Warmup Enrichment - Alternate Mode
table.description: Starting enrichment for this factory-selected bank. The higher cold-start or warmup state is used, then fades with its matching decrement. At coolant temperatures of 203 degF or higher, separate hot-start values replace this curve. Used only when the alternate enrichment mode is selected.

table.name: Warmup Enrichment Decrement
table.description: Amount removed from this enrichment state once per full 720-degree engine cycle after cranking. Larger values make it fade faster; elapsed time depends on RPM. At coolant temperatures of 203 degF or higher, separate hot-start values replace this curve.

table.name: Warmup Enrichment Decrement - Alternate Mode
table.description: Amount removed from this enrichment state once per full 720-degree engine cycle after cranking. Larger values make it fade faster; elapsed time depends on RPM. At coolant temperatures of 203 degF or higher, separate hot-start values replace this curve. Used only when the alternate enrichment mode is selected.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Cold Limit
table.description: Pressure ceiling while the cold-start hold is active. Uses the colder stored intake-air temperature. The ceiling recovers toward the overall maximum after the hold ends.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Cold Limit Hold Time
table.description: Time to retain the cold-start pressure limit after the start state ends. Uses the colder stored intake-air temperature.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Cold Limit Recovery Rate
table.description: Rate at which the cold-start pressure ceiling rises toward the overall maximum after the hold ends. Applied in 25 ms steps.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Overall Max
table.description: Overall fuel pressure limit. An alternate temperature-based limit can also apply.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Target 1
table.description: Alternate target used by the qualified hot-restart pressure state. Takes priority over the after-start and other alternate targets. The active pressure ceiling still applies.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Target 2
table.description: Alternate pressure target for qualified startup and temperature-difference states. Its companion alternate bank is used when injection-phase qualification is active. Hot-restart and after-start targets take priority. The active pressure ceiling still applies.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Target 2 - Alternate Bank
table.description: Companion alternate pressure target used when startup conditions and injection-phase qualification are active. Hot-restart and after-start targets take priority. The active pressure ceiling still applies.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Target 3
table.description: One of two normal pressure targets. Keep its companion alternate bank consistent unless a mode-specific change is intended. Temperature corrections, blending and the active pressure ceiling still apply.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Target 3 - Alternate Bank
table.description: Companion normal pressure target selected by the pressure-control mode. Keep it consistent with Fuel Pressure Target 3 unless a mode-specific change is intended. Temperature corrections, blending and the active pressure ceiling still apply.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Target 4 - After Start
table.description: Alternate pressure target during the qualified after-start hold. Hot-restart pressure takes priority. The active pressure ceiling still applies.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Target - Deceleration
table.description: Pressure target during qualified deceleration. Selection follows the fuel-cut RPM and load conditions and returns to normal pressure control when qualification clears. The active pressure ceiling still applies.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Target Blend Rate
table.description: Rate of return from the alternate pressure target toward normal pressure control. Higher values blend faster. Applied in 25 ms steps.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Target Temperature Correction Multiplier
table.description: Scales the selected startup pressure target by RPM and coolant temperature. A value of 1 leaves it unchanged. Applies to both startup target banks; hot-restart, after-start and normal pressure targets bypass this multiplier. The active pressure ceiling still applies.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Correction Maximum
table.description: Highest allowed combined pump fuel-demand correction. Zero is neutral; positive values increase the pump fuel-demand index.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Correction Minimum
table.description: Lowest allowed combined pump fuel-demand correction. Zero is neutral; positive values increase the pump fuel-demand index.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Integral Correction Maximum
table.description: Highest allowed accumulated pump fuel-demand correction. Zero is neutral; positive values increase the pump fuel-demand index.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Integral Correction Minimum
table.description: Lowest allowed accumulated pump fuel-demand correction. Zero is neutral; positive values increase the pump fuel-demand index.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Integral Deadband - Lower
table.description: Lower pressure-error boundary for updating accumulated correction. The accumulator holds inside the deadband.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Integral Deadband - Upper
table.description: Upper pressure-error boundary for updating accumulated correction. Error is actual pressure minus target.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Integral Error Limit - Lower
table.description: Lower error limit for updating accumulated correction. The accumulator holds at or below this limit.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Integral Error Limit - Upper
table.description: Upper error limit for updating accumulated correction. The accumulator holds at or above this limit.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Integral Step
table.description: Change in accumulated fuel-demand correction per qualifying control event. Higher values change the correction faster. The ECU applies half-count rounding.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Proportional Correction Maximum
table.description: Highest allowed proportional pump fuel-demand correction. Zero is neutral; positive values increase the pump fuel-demand index.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Proportional Correction Minimum
table.description: Lowest allowed proportional pump fuel-demand correction. Zero is neutral; positive values increase the pump fuel-demand index.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Proportional Deadband - Lower
table.description: Lower pressure-error boundary for applying proportional correction. No proportional correction is applied inside the deadband.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Proportional Deadband - Upper
table.description: Upper pressure-error boundary for applying proportional correction. Error is actual pressure minus target.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Proportional Gain
table.description: Immediate fuel-demand correction per MPa of pressure error. Higher values respond more strongly. Positive correction increases the pump fuel-demand index.

table.name: Fuel Pressure High Limit Monitor Delay
table.description: Time above the cold-limit monitor ceiling before the high-pressure performance test fails. Counts down in 25 ms steps while its qualifying conditions remain true.

table.name: Fuel Pressure High Limit Monitor Margin
table.description: Effective pressure margin above the active cold-start pressure ceiling used by the high-pressure performance monitor.

table.name: Fuel Pressure Sensor Fault Substitute
table.description: Substitute pressure used for injector calculations when the pressure sensor is unavailable. Pressure feedback correction is reset separately during a sensor fault.

table.name: Fuel Pump Base Phase - 1 Low Pressure
table.description: Base pump-valve phase by RPM and fuel-demand index. Blended with adjacent pressure banks. Delay compensation and the phase minimum apply afterward. Fuel-demand index uses the ECU lookup scale.

table.name: Fuel Pump Base Phase - 2 Reference Pressure
table.description: Base pump-valve phase by RPM and fuel-demand index. Blended with adjacent pressure banks. Delay compensation and the phase minimum apply afterward. Fuel-demand index uses the ECU lookup scale.

table.name: Fuel Pump Base Phase - 3 High Pressure
table.description: Base pump-valve phase by RPM and fuel-demand index. Blended with adjacent pressure banks. Delay compensation and the phase minimum apply afterward. Fuel-demand index uses the ECU lookup scale.

table.name: Fuel Pump Pressure Anchor - 1 Low
table.description: Pressure used to blend the pump base-phase banks. Keep the low, reference and high anchors in increasing order.

table.name: Fuel Pump Pressure Anchor - 2 Reference
table.description: Pressure used to blend the pump base-phase banks. Keep the low, reference and high anchors in increasing order.

table.name: Fuel Pump Pressure Anchor - 3 High
table.description: Pressure used to blend the pump base-phase banks. Keep the low, reference and high anchors in increasing order.

table.name: Fuel Pump Valve Delay Compensation
table.description: Electrical delay allowed for the pump valve. Advances the electrical command and is added to the total energization limit.

table.name: Fuel Pump Valve Hold Duration Limit
table.description: Hold-time allowance after valve delay compensation. The ECU adds delay compensation to set the total energization ceiling; available pump phase can shorten the pulse.

table.name: Fuel Pump Valve Peak Duration Limit
table.description: Maximum initial energization time for the pump valve. Limited to the actual total pulse duration.

table.name: Injector Capacity Load Margin
table.description: Load subtracted from the calculated injection-capacity ceiling. Higher values reduce allowable load without changing injector pulsewidth. The factory capacity calculation and other load limits still apply.

table.name: Injection Capacity End Phase Minimum
table.description: Minimum end phase used to calculate available injection capacity. Higher values reduce the phase window and calculated load ceiling. This is a capacity-calculation limit; it does not directly set the main injection-phase target.

table.name: Injection Phase - Base
table.description: Electrical end-of-injection target before blending and retard corrections. Measured before compression TDC; larger values move injection earlier.

table.name: Injection Phase - Startup
table.description: Electrical end-of-injection target during the timed startup states. Takes priority over warm and blended targets. Larger values move injection earlier.

table.name: Injection Phase - Transition
table.description: Electrical end-of-injection target approached as the blend weight rises. Pulsewidth and the start-phase maximum can move the actual end later.

table.name: Injection Phase - Warm
table.description: Electrical end-of-injection target selected by the stored coolant warm-mode threshold. Startup timing takes priority. Larger values move injection earlier.

table.name: Injection Phase Blend Rate
table.description: Transition weight gained per second, in 25 ms steps. Higher values blend faster. A rate of 0.05 takes about 20 seconds to move from zero to full transition weight.

table.name: Injection Phase Fixed Value
table.description: Electrical end-of-injection target used with the fixed override. Bypasses map selection and phase corrections. Pulsewidth and the start-phase maximum still apply.

table.name: Injection Phase Fixed Value Enable
table.description: Enables the fixed injection phase value in place of the phase maps.

table.name: Injection Phase Minimum
table.description: Latest allowed electrical end-of-injection phase before compression TDC. Larger values keep injection farther before TDC.

table.name: Injection Phase Retard - After Start
table.description: Retards the end-phase target after the start state ends. Higher values move the target later. The fixed-value override bypasses this correction.

table.name: Injection Phase Retard - Coolant
table.description: Retards the end-phase target by coolant temperature and RPM. Higher values move the target later. The fixed-value override bypasses this correction.

table.name: Injection Phase Temperature Correction
table.description: Temperature correction added to transition phase before blending. Positive values increase commanded phase.

table.name: Injection Phase Temperature Correction Multiplier
table.description: Scales the temperature-based phase correction by RPM and load.

table.name: Injection Phase Warm Mode Hysteresis
table.description: Coolant-temperature drop below the warm-mode threshold needed to leave the Transition injection-phase map and return to the normal blend.

table.name: Injection Phase Warm Mode Temperature
table.description: Current coolant temperature above which the Transition injection-phase map is selected. Startup phase selection and the fixed-phase override take priority.

table.name: Injection Start Phase Maximum
table.description: Earliest allowed injection start. A longer pulse moves injection end later once this limit is reached. Measured before compression TDC; larger values are earlier.

table.name: Injector Base Pulsewidth - 1
table.description: Increase to lengthen the calculated injector pulse at the same fuel quantity. Used by the alternate selector. Values are encoded coefficients, not milliseconds.

table.name: Injector Base Pulsewidth - 2
table.description: Increase to lengthen the calculated injector pulse at the same fuel quantity. Used when curve 1 is unselected.

table.name: Injector Pulsewidth Minimum
table.description: Minimum pulsewidth by fuel pressure, applied before short-pulse correction and the pressure-dependent offset.

table.name: Injector Pulsewidth Offset
table.description: Pressure-dependent pulse-width adjustment after short-pulse correction. Larger values lengthen the commanded pulse.

table.name: Injector Short Pulsewidth Correction
table.description: Corrects base pulse width for injector nonlinearity. Values above one lengthen the pulse.

table.name: Closed Loop Open Loop Load Threshold 1
table.description: Load threshold by RPM that triggers transition to open-loop fueling.

table.name: Closed Loop Open Loop Load Threshold 2
table.description: Load threshold by RPM that triggers transition to open-loop fueling.

table.name: Closed Loop Open Loop Load Threshold 3
table.description: Load threshold by RPM that triggers transition to open-loop fueling.

table.name: Closed Loop Open Loop Load Threshold 4
table.description: Load threshold by RPM that triggers transition to open-loop fueling.

table.name: Effective Final Drive - 1st - 4th
table.description: Effective final-drive ratio used by the ECU gear estimate for 1st through 4th gears.

table.name: Effective Final Drive - 5th - 6th
table.description: Effective final-drive ratio used by the ECU gear estimate for 5th, 6th and reverse.

table.name: Gear Ratio - 1st
table.description: Transmission ratio for 1st gear.

table.name: Gear Ratio - 2nd
table.description: Transmission ratio for 2nd gear.

table.name: Gear Ratio - 3rd
table.description: Transmission ratio for 3rd gear.

table.name: Gear Ratio - 4th
table.description: Transmission ratio for 4th gear.

table.name: Gear Ratio - 5th
table.description: Transmission ratio for 5th gear.

table.name: Gear Ratio - 6th
table.description: Transmission ratio for 6th gear.

table.name: Gear Ratio - Reverse
table.description: Reverse-gear ratio used for gear recognition.

table.name: Idle Ignition Timing Adjustment Desired RPM Correction - In Gear
table.description: Idle spark correction by RPM error, before limits. Positive values advance timing; negative values retard timing.

table.name: Idle Ignition Timing Adjustment Desired RPM Correction - Neutral 1
table.description: Idle spark correction in the alternate neutral mode. Positive values advance timing; negative values retard timing. The factory mode selector and correction floor still apply.

table.name: Idle Ignition Timing Adjustment Desired RPM Correction - Neutral 2
table.description: Idle spark correction by RPM error, before limits. Positive values advance timing; negative values retard timing.

table.name: Idle Ignition Timing Adjustment Desired RPM Correction - Neutral 3
table.description: Idle spark correction by RPM error, before limits. Positive values advance timing; negative values retard timing.

table.name: Idle Ignition Timing Correction Floor 1
table.description: Minimum idle spark correction by coolant temperature, before other timing limits.

table.name: Idle Ignition Timing Correction Floor 2
table.description: Minimum idle spark correction by coolant temperature, before other timing limits.

table.name: Idle RPM - AC ON - In Gear
table.description: Minimum idle RPM by barometric pressure with A/C on.

table.name: Idle RPM - AC ON - Neutral
table.description: Minimum idle RPM by barometric pressure with A/C on.

table.name: Idle RPM - In Gear
table.description: Normal in-gear idle target by current and stored coolant temperature. Factory mode qualification, added idle compensation and target limits still apply.

table.name: Idle RPM - Neutral
table.description: Normal neutral/unloaded idle target by current and stored coolant temperature. Factory mode qualification, added idle compensation and target limits still apply.

table.name: Idle Transition Spark Retard - Base
table.description: Base spark-retard amount during a qualified idle transition. Uses the load rise since the transition reference was captured. RPM multipliers and the factory ramp limit still apply.

table.name: Idle Transition Spark Retard - RPM Error Multiplier
Engine Speed Minus Target Idle Speed (RPM)

table.description: Scales idle transition spark retard by current RPM minus target idle RPM.

table.name: Idle Transition Spark Retard - RPM Multiplier
table.description: Scales idle-transition spark retard using engine speed captured at the qualifying transition. A value of 1 leaves the base amount unchanged. The RPM-error multiplier also applies.

table.name: Abnormal Max Ignition Timing
table.description: Maximum permitted ignition timing indexed by load and engine speed under abnormal operating conditions. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Closed Loop Base Timing Abnormal
table.description: Closed-loop endpoint of the ignition blend for abnormal without overload mode. Higher values add advance. Blend weight controls its contribution; mode flags select the bank. Above 4000 RPM, this lookup holds its last column.

table.name: Closed Loop Base Timing Abnormal Overload
table.description: Closed-loop endpoint of the ignition blend for abnormal and overload mode. Higher values add advance. Blend weight controls its contribution; mode flags select the bank. Above 4000 RPM, this lookup holds its last column.

table.name: Closed Loop Base Timing Normal
table.description: Closed-loop endpoint of the ignition blend for normal without overload mode. Higher values add advance. Blend weight controls its contribution; mode flags select the bank. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Closed Loop Base Timing Normal Overload
table.description: Closed-loop endpoint of the ignition blend for normal and overload mode. Higher values add advance. Blend weight controls its contribution; mode flags select the bank. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Closed Loop Max Ignition Timing
table.description: Maximum closed-loop ignition timing under normal conditions; blended with open-loop timing during transition. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: High BAT/ECT Retard - Abnormal Mode
table.description: Temperature-based retard for abnormal ignition mode, selected alongside abnormal base-timing maps. Higher positive values remove more timing. RPM/load multipliers scale the retard. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: High BAT/ECT Retard - Normal Mode
table.description: Temperature-based retard for normal ignition mode, selected alongside normal base-timing maps. Higher positive values remove more timing. RPM/load multipliers scale the retard. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: High BAT/ECT Retard Multiplier 1
table.description: First endpoint of the RPM/load multiplier blend for temperature retard. A value of 1 leaves retard unchanged; higher values increase retard. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: High BAT/ECT Retard Multiplier 2
table.description: Second endpoint of the RPM/load multiplier blend for temperature retard. A value of 1 leaves retard unchanged; higher values increase retard. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Ignition Coolant and Load Correction
table.description: Ignition timing correction by coolant temperature and load. Positive values advance timing; negative values retard it. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Ignition Coolant Correction - Alternate
table.description: Adds timing by coolant temperature in the alternate correction mode, before other timing limits. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Ignition Coolant Correction - Transition
table.description: Temporary coolant-based ignition correction after a qualifying mode change. Positive values add timing advance. The factory hold and recovery still apply; final timing limits remain active.

table.name: Knock Retard Additive
table.description: Offset added to the knock-detection reference: base reference × Knock Retard Multiplier + this offset. This is in ECU knock-signal units and does not directly remove degrees of ignition timing. A qualified factory mode halves this offset. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Knock Retard Decrement Step Size 3
table.description: Amount of knock retard removed at each qualified recovery step in this mode. Larger values restore timing faster. Recovery Interval - 1 controls the step spacing. This ROM uses a single value instead of an RPM/load table.

table.name: Knock Retard Gain - Alternate Strategy
table.description: Gain for the calculated knock-retard step when the alternate strategy is selected. The supplied ROM uses the factory strategy, which bypasses this value. Higher values increase the step for the same relative knock-signal excess. This ROM uses a single value instead of an RPM/load table.

table.name: Knock Retard Limit
table.description: Limit for knock-retard increases by engine speed. Lowering it may not immediately reduce existing retard. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Knock Retard Multiplier
table.description: Multiplier for the knock-detection reference, not accumulated spark retard. The reference is base reference × this multiplier + Knock Retard Additive. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Knock Retard Recovery Interval - 1
table.description: Time between qualified recovery steps using Knock Retard Decrement Step Size 3. Counts down in 10 ms steps, so the effective interval rounds up to the next 10 ms.

table.name: Knock Retard Recovery Interval - 2
table.description: Time between qualified recovery steps in the second recovery mode. Counts down in 10 ms steps, so the effective interval rounds up to the next 10 ms. This mode uses a fixed recovery amount.

table.name: Knock Retard Threshold Max RPM
table.description: Upper engine-speed threshold for the knock-retard operating window. A separate mode can override it.

table.name: Knock Retard Threshold Min ECT
table.description: Minimum coolant temperature for this knock-retard operating mode.

table.name: Knock Retard Threshold Min Load 1
table.description: Minimum load for this knock-retard mode at each engine speed. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Knock Retard Threshold Min Load 2
table.description: Minimum load for this knock-retard mode at each engine speed. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Knock Retard Threshold Min RPM
table.description: Lower engine-speed threshold for the knock-retard operating window.

table.name: Open Loop Base Timing Abnormal
table.description: Open-loop endpoint of the ignition blend for abnormal without overload mode. Higher values add advance. Blend weight controls its contribution; mode flags select the bank. Above 4000 RPM, this lookup holds its last column.

table.name: Open Loop Base Timing Abnormal - Additional Enrichment
table.description: Timing bank for additional fuel enrichment beyond the normal open-loop reference. Blended by requested lambda; normal, abnormal and overload selections still apply.

table.name: Open Loop Base Timing Abnormal Overload
table.description: Open-loop endpoint of the ignition blend for abnormal and overload mode. Higher values add advance. Blend weight controls its contribution; mode flags select the bank. Above 4000 RPM, this lookup holds its last column.

table.name: Open Loop Base Timing Abnormal Overload - Additional Enrichment
table.description: Timing bank for additional fuel enrichment beyond the normal open-loop reference. Blended by requested lambda; normal, abnormal and overload selections still apply.

table.name: Open Loop Base Timing Normal
table.description: Open-loop endpoint of the ignition blend for normal without overload mode. Higher values add advance. Blend weight controls its contribution; mode flags select the bank. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Open Loop Base Timing Normal - Additional Enrichment
table.description: Timing bank for additional fuel enrichment beyond the normal open-loop reference. Blended by requested lambda; normal, abnormal and overload selections still apply.

table.name: Open Loop Base Timing Normal Overload
table.description: Open-loop endpoint of the ignition blend for normal and overload mode. Higher values add advance. Blend weight controls its contribution; mode flags select the bank. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Open Loop Base Timing Normal Overload - Additional Enrichment
table.description: Timing bank for additional fuel enrichment beyond the normal open-loop reference. Blended by requested lambda; normal, abnormal and overload selections still apply.

table.name: Open Loop Max Ignition Timing
table.description: Maximum permitted open-loop ignition timing by load and RPM, blended with the closed-loop table during transition. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Overload Retard
table.description: Positive values remove timing; negative values add timing while this correction is enabled. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Supplemental Spark Retard - Load
table.description: Adds a retard request by load when enabled. The largest competing request applies before other timing limits. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Timed Load-Based Ignition Retard
table.description: Load-based ignition retard while its timer and latch allow. Warm-engine open-loop operation can inhibit it. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: APP Requested Load Knocking
table.description: Requested load for knock-related mode by RPM and pedal position. Overload takes priority over knock-related mode. Higher values request more load; final load ceilings still apply. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: APP Requested Load Normal
table.description: Requested load for normal mode by RPM and pedal position. Overload takes priority over knock-related mode. Higher values request more load; final load ceilings still apply. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: APP Requested Load Overload
table.description: Requested load for overload mode by RPM and pedal position. Overload takes priority over knock-related mode. Higher values request more load; final load ceilings still apply. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: BCS DC Adjustment - Load Target Correction - Incremental
table.description: Added to accumulated duty correction each controller update, from actual load minus target load. Positive values add duty; negative values subtract duty. Accumulated and combined limits apply. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: BCS DC Adjustment - Load Target Correction - Initial
table.description: Initial duty-point correction from actual load minus target load. Positive values add duty; negative values subtract duty. Combined correction limits apply. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Per Gear Requested Load - Temperature Blend End
table.description: Temperature where per-gear load limits fully use the high-temperature curves.

table.name: Per Gear Requested Load - Temperature Blend Start
table.description: Temperature where per-gear load limits start blending from the low-temperature curves toward the high-temperature curves.

table.name: Requested Load - 1st Gear Limit High BAT
table.description: Requested load limit for first gear with high boost air temperature. Blends from the low temperature limit.

table.name: Requested Load - 1st Gear Limit Low BAT
table.description: Requested load limit for first gear with low boost air temperature. Blends toward the high temperature limit.

table.name: Requested Load - 2nd Gear Limit High BAT
table.description: Requested load limit for second gear with high boost air temperature. Blends from the low temperature limit.

table.name: Requested Load - 2nd Gear Limit Low BAT
table.description: Requested load limit for second gear with low boost air temperature. Blends toward the high temperature limit.

table.name: Requested Load - 3rd Gear Limit High BAT
table.description: Requested load limit for third gear with high boost air temperature. Blends from the low temperature limit.

table.name: Requested Load - 3rd Gear Limit Low BAT
table.description: Requested load limit for third gear with low boost air temperature. Blends toward the high temperature limit.

table.name: Requested Load - 4th Gear Limit High BAT
table.description: Requested load limit for fourth gear with high boost air temperature. Blends from the low temperature limit.

table.name: Requested Load - 4th Gear Limit Low BAT
table.description: Requested load limit for fourth gear with low boost air temperature. Blends toward the high temperature limit.

table.name: Requested Load - 5th Gear Limit High BAT
table.description: Requested load limit for fifth gear with high boost air temperature. Blends from the low temperature limit.

table.name: Requested Load - 5th Gear Limit Low BAT
table.description: Requested load limit for fifth gear with low boost air temperature. Blends toward the high temperature limit.

table.name: Requested Load - 6th Gear Limit High BAT
table.description: Requested load limit for sixth gear with high boost air temperature. Blends from the low temperature limit.

table.name: Requested Load - 6th Gear Limit Low BAT
table.description: Requested load limit for sixth gear with low boost air temperature. Blends toward the high temperature limit.

table.name: Requested Load Limit Overall
table.description: Shared load ceiling used when the RPM-dependent limit is not qualified. Gear, barometric and other downstream limits can reduce requested load further.

table.name: Requested Load Limit RPM
table.description: Conditional RPM-based requested-load ceiling. Bypassed by this ROM's stock manual-transmission configuration.

table.name: Requested Load Limits Baro Specific
table.description: Requested-load limit by RPM and barometric pressure. Uses the lowest-pressure row during a barometric fault. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Requested Load Transient Multiplier - 1st Gear
table.description: Requested-load multiplier during qualified gear transitions. Uses current and retained RPM. Lower values reduce load; 1.0 leaves it unchanged. This ROM shares each bank across its factory gear-selection paths.

table.name: Requested Load Transient Multiplier - 2nd Gear
table.description: Requested-load multiplier during qualified gear transitions. Uses current and retained RPM. Lower values reduce load; 1.0 leaves it unchanged. This ROM shares each bank across its factory gear-selection paths.

table.name: Requested Load Transient Multiplier - 3rd Gear
table.description: Requested-load multiplier during qualified gear transitions. Uses current and retained RPM. Lower values reduce load; 1.0 leaves it unchanged. This ROM shares each bank across its factory gear-selection paths.

table.name: Requested Load Transient Multiplier - 4th Gear (Alternate Configuration)
table.description: Requested-load multiplier during qualified gear transitions. Uses current and retained RPM. Lower values reduce load; 1.0 leaves it unchanged. This ROM shares each bank across its factory gear-selection paths. The fourth-gear bank is bypassed by the normal gear path and is used only by the alternate configuration.

table.name: Volumetric Efficiency
table.description: Base volumetric-efficiency ratio used by the factory load model. Higher values raise modeled load in this path. The VVT modifier, factory overrides and load ceilings still apply.

table.name: Volumetric Efficiency - VVT Modifier
table.description: Adds to the base volumetric-efficiency ratio through the factory VVT blend. Zero adds no correction. Applied only while the VVT mode is qualified and its inhibit is clear.

table.name: MAF Airflow Floor
table.description: Sets the airflow floor used by the normal MAF calculation. Previously higher floors decay toward this value.

table.name: MAF Calibration
table.description: Airflow represented by each MAF sensor voltage. The same curve is used during initialization and normal operation. Keep the upper range within the sensor and housing capacity.

table.name: High RPM Shift Retard - RPM
table.description: Engine-speed adjustment to the high-RPM shift-retard correction.

table.name: High RPM Shift Retard - RPM vs. Gear
table.description: Limits shift retard by engine speed and gear.

table.name: High RPM Shift Retard APP Threshold
table.description: Minimum captured pedal position for reloading shift timer 1. RPM must also meet its per-gear threshold, and a new qualified shift-input event must be present.

table.name: High RPM Shift Retard Correction Threshold - Base
table.description: Ignition-correction threshold that starts timer 2. RPM, pedal and other shift conditions also apply.

table.name: High RPM Shift Retard Correction Threshold - Hysteresis
table.description: Correction drop below the base that clears timer 2. Its normal engine-event countdown still applies.

table.name: High RPM Shift Retard Multiplier
table.description: Scales shift retard by captured gear and engine-event counter. One event spans 180 crank degrees, so elapsed time varies with RPM. Other correction limits still apply.

table.name: High RPM Shift Retard Multiplier - Alternate Mode
table.description: Shift-retard multiplier by engine-event counter when the per-gear multiplier mode is not selected. One event spans 180 crank degrees; elapsed time varies with RPM. Other shift correction limits still apply.

table.name: High RPM Shift Retard RPM Threshold - Base
table.description: RPM needed to start timer 1 on a clutch press above the pedal threshold. Timer reload must be nonzero.

table.name: High RPM Shift Retard RPM Threshold - Hysteresis
table.description: RPM drop below the base that clears timer 1. Its normal engine-event countdown still applies.

table.name: High RPM Shift Retard Timer - 1
table.description: Timer 1 reload in 180-degree crank events. Approximate duration is events times 30 divided by RPM, in seconds, while countdown conditions remain true. Zero prevents a sustained active state.

table.name: High RPM Shift Retard Timer - 2
table.description: Timer 2 reload in 180-degree crank events. Approximate duration is events times 30 divided by RPM, in seconds, while countdown conditions remain true. Zero prevents a sustained active state.

table.name: Catalyst Temperature Model - Enrichment Additive
table.description: Temperature adjustment to the catalyst-temperature model as fuel enrichment changes.

table.name: DBW Throttle Knock
table.description: Knock-related-mode throttle target by RPM and corrected load. Higher values request more opening. Overload takes priority over knock-related mode. Density/temperature corrections shift the lookup; later limits apply. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: DBW Throttle Normal
table.description: Normal-mode throttle target by RPM and corrected load. Higher values request more opening. Overload takes priority over knock-related mode. Density/temperature corrections shift the lookup; later limits apply. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: DBW Throttle Overload
table.description: Overload-mode throttle target by RPM and corrected load. Higher values request more opening. Overload takes priority over knock-related mode. Density/temperature corrections shift the lookup; later limits apply. Uses nearest edge outside axes.

table.name: Intake Cam Advance (VVT)
table.description: Base intake-cam advance target by RPM and load. Higher values request more advance. A correction weight scales this target; state and high-RPM overrides can replace it. Uses nearest edge outside axes.
